name: iContact
summary: Straightforward email marketing for growing businesses. Build campaigns and automations with drag-and-drop design and deliverability support.
best_for: small businesses and nonprofits who want a simple, reliable email tool with strong deliverability and a real marketing advisor included on every paid plan
skip_if: you need advanced multi-branch automation (ActiveCampaign does more) or you're chasing the rock-bottom cheapest option
honest_knock: Pricing feels a touch high for what you get, and the Standard plan's hard caps on automations and landing pages push growing teams to upgrade sooner than expected. Set against ActiveCampaign the automation builder is the thinner half of the deal; what iContact sells instead is a product you can hold in your head, deliverability that holds up, and a human on support included rather than sold as a tier.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-29, every contact band read on their own pricing page; previously verified 2026-08-17) No permanent free plan: a 30-day free trial, then from $9 a month for Standard at 500 contacts, with 15% off for paying yearly. At 500 contacts Standard is $9 a month, Premium $16 and Ultimate $24; Standard then climbs through $14, $28, $45, $73, $110, $180, $250 and $350 at the 1,000, 2,500, 5,000, 10,000, 15,000, 25,000, 35,000 and 50,000-contact bands. Premium steps through $27, $41, $73, $109, $159, $229, $309 and $399 at the same bands. Ultimate steps through $38, $53, $84, $128, $183, $258, $338 and $427. Standard covers templates, landing pages and automations; Premium adds unlimited users, social posting and the AI content assistant; Ultimate adds email verification, dynamic content and AI templates and images. Larger lists are quoted.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested iContact on a 30 day trial: an AI generated newsletter draft and the plan and price screens. Nothing was sent and no contact was added. Create Message offered templates (Information, Promotion, Feedback, Occasion, Event, Reminder), Plain-Text, HTML Editor, Generate with AI and Start from Scratch. Generate with AI was used with the prompt Monthly newsletter for a small animal shelter: thank volunteers, announce the winter food drive on 6 December, and ask readers to donate. and the length Short, then a template (the first was a Thanksgiving template), the question Preserve Images? answered with Replace Images, and a preview appeared after about 20 seconds. The text matched the prompt: it thanks the volunteers, says Mark your calendars! Our annual Winter Food Drive takes place on 6 December and mentions essential meals and cozy blankets for our furry friends. The images the AI chose did not fit: a tortoise on its back at the top and a photo of avocados and limes next to the food drive text. Use Message opened the drag and drop editor with the blocks Text, Image, GIF, Caption, Collage, Video, Button, Add to Calendar, Divider, HTML and Saved Block, with Last saved at 5:14pm. The subject line was empty and Generate Subject Line carries the label PREMIUM. From Create Message to an editable draft took about 2.5 minutes. Nothing was sent, because a CAN-SPAM address and a list were still needed, and no contact was added. Automation and a second login were not looked at. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The AI chose images that did not fit the text, and the plan selection screen opened with a paid add on already selected.

sessions.what: We built an AI-generated newsletter draft in iContact's 30-day trial on 13 November 2026 and read the plan and price screens. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We sent nothing and added no contact. We did not open the automation tools.
findings: The Create Message screen lists six template groups, plain text, an HTML editor, an AI option and a blank start. We took the AI option with a brief for a fictional animal shelter: thank volunteers, announce a winter food drive on 6 December, ask readers to donate. Length: Short.

After choosing a template and answering 'Preserve Images?' with Replace Images, a preview appeared in about 20 seconds. The text matched the brief: it thanks the volunteers and announces the food drive on 6 December.
The images the AI chose did not fit. A tortoise on its back sat at the top, and a photo of avocados and limes stood next to the food drive text.

Accepting the draft opened a drag-and-drop editor with eleven block types, from text and image to a calendar button and saved blocks. From Create Message to an editable draft took about 2.5 minutes (our approximate timing). The subject line was empty, and Generate Subject Line carries a PREMIUM label.

We could not send. The editor still wanted a CAN-SPAM address and a list. The dashboard showed '30 days left in your trial', no card was requested, and the trial limits were 100 contacts and 200 emails.

On the Update My Account screen, a Dynamic Content add-on at $6 a month was already selected when it opened. Standard costs $9 a month at 500 contacts and $73 at 10,000. The screen totals of $22 (Premium, 500 contacts) and $79 (Standard, 10,000 contacts) include the add-on. Annual billing is labelled 'save 15%'. We did not reach payment, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.
